resale_co.name: Certificate of Compliance (COC) / Temporary Certificate of Compliance (TCOC), Residential Resale Inspection (Township Code Chapter 186)
resale_co.issued_by: Construction & Zoning Office / Code Official (Township Annex, 10 Reeve Ave.)
resale_co.lead_time: Application in and paid at least 14 business days before closing; inspections Mondays and Wednesdays 8 to 10 AM
resale_co.valid_for: 6 months (if the sale does not happen within 6 months a new application, fee and inspection are required)
requirements: Interior and exterior inspection under the township Land Use code, International Property Maintenance Code and NJ fire code; includes the smoke/CO (CSDCMAC) check
House numbers: numerals only, at least 4 inches, contrasting color, on the house (not doors or mailboxes)

Smoke alarms on every level on the ceiling, at the base of basement stairs, within 10 feet of all bedrooms; no more than 10 years old; 10-year sealed battery where battery units are allowed; hardwired alarms cannot be replaced with battery alarms
CO alarm in the hallway within 10 feet of all bedrooms, less than 10 years old
Thumb-turn locks on all exit doors; no keyed locks on the egress side
Gutters, downspouts with splash blocks, roof, soffit, fascia, siding and paint in good repair
Guardrails on porches, decks and landings over 30 inches; handrails on steps with 3 or more risers
Sidewalk, driveway and apron level with no trip hazards; replacement rather than patching
GFCI outlets trip; outlet, switch and junction box covers in place; electrical panel covered, no open spaces, circuits labeled
Faucets hot on left, cold on right, no leaks; sink strainers; stove anti-tip device
Sump pump discharges outside, not into the sanitary sewer; water meter installed and accessible
Metal dryer vent; proper water heater and furnace venting; water heater bonding; oil heat emergency shut-off switch with red label
Attached garage walls/ceiling next to living space drywalled and taped
Bathroom window or working exhaust fan; screens installed
Pool barrier 5 to 6 feet with self-closing, self-latching gate
All permitted work must have final inspections and a Certificate of Approval (heater, water heater, finished basement, roof, siding, deck, etc.)

fees.label: COC application more than 14 business days before change of ownership
fees.quote: For COC applications submitted more than 14 business days prior to the date change of ownership occurs or the date of change of occupancy, the fee is $150

fees.label: COC application more than 7 but less than 13 business days before
fees.quote: For COC applications submitted more than 7 business days but less than 13 business days prior to the date of change of ownership occurs or the date of change of occupancy, the fee is $175.

fees.label: COC application more than 4 but less than 6 business days before
fees.quote: For COC applications submitted more than 4 business days but less than 6 business days prior to the date of change of ownership occurs or the date of change of occupancy, the fee is $200.

fees.label: COC application less than 4 business days before
fees.quote: For COC applications submitted less than 4 business days prior to the date of change of ownership occurs or the date of change of occupancy, the fee is $225.

fees.label: COC application after the change of ownership
fees.quote: For COC applications submitted after the date change of ownership occurs or the date of change of occupancy, the fee is $250.

fees.label: Re-inspection (paid before re-inspection is scheduled)
fees.quote: Re-Inspection fee of $25.00 will be collected for additional inspections, prior to re-inspection being scheduled.

fees.label: First re-inspection after a Temporary COC
fees.quote: The fee for the first re-inspection after issuance of a TCOC is $25.

fees.label: Second re-inspection after a Temporary COC
fees.quote: The fee for the second re-inspection after issuance of a TCOC is $50.

fees.label: Third re-inspection after a Temporary COC
fees.quote: The fee for the third re-inspection after issuance of a TCOC is $75.

fees.label: Fourth or later re-inspection after a Temporary COC, each
fees.quote: The fee for a fourth or subsequent re-inspection after issuance of a TCOC is $100 for each such re-inspection.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Download the Residential Resale / Tenant Change Inspection Application (PDF) or use the township's online GovPilot form (https://main.govpilot.com/web/public/474cdd15-dbc_Rental-Resale-Township-of-Haddon?uid=7071&ust=NJ&pu=1&id=0). Submit it with a check or money order payable to 'Township of Haddon' to the Annex Building, 10 Reeve Ave., at least 14 business days before closing. Questions: Ryan Sheppard, rsheppard@haddontwp.com.

evidence.quote: A Residential Property Inspection MUST be completed and a COC or Temporary COC MUST be issued PRIOR to closing per Township of Haddon Municipal Code Chapter 186-6 Article 3B.
If a COC or Temp COC is not issued prior to closing, a $2,500 fine may be issued to the buyer, seller and realtors.
If the change does not occur within six (6) months, a new application, fee & inspection will be required.
All applications must be in and paid for at least 14 business days in advance of closing date.
All Property Resale Inspections are done on Mondays and Wednesdays from 8:00 AM - 10:00 AM.
Ryan Sheppard Resale Inspector Ext. 6276 rsheppard@haddontwp.com
a certificate of compliance (COC) shall be required prior to the change of ownership or change of occupancy of any residential property

Applications filed pursuant to this article shall be delivered to the enforcing officer not less than 30 days prior to the date that the property is scheduled to be sold or occupied by a new tenant/occupant.
A TCOC may be issued for a period not to exceed 60 days, in the sole discretion of the enforcing officer.

resale_co.notes: Fee tiers are quoted from the Chapter 111 fee amendment printed on the township's June 2026 form. New this check: Chapter 186 and Section 111-42 of the township code were read through the ecode360 print view. The code version of the fee tiers says 'days' (not business days) and closes the gaps the form leaves: more than 14 days $150, more than 7 but less than 14 days $175, more than 4 but less than 7 days $200, less than 4 days $225, after the change of ownership $250 (same amounts as the form). Section 186-6 says applications go in not less than 30 days before the sale, while the form and web page ask for 14 business days; ask which the office uses. A Temporary COC needs a notarized buyer letter, allows no move-in, and lasts no more than 60 days (Section 186-9). Rentals have extra lead-based paint rules ($100 if the township does the visual inspection, $20 if a private report is submitted); these do not apply to owner sales. Code Official's office for checklist questions: 856-833-6276. Construction inspections: inspections@haddontwp.com. The online GovPilot version of the form is linked from the Construction & Zoning page.

requirements: Smoke alarms on every level on the ceiling, at the base of basement stairs and within 10 feet of all bedrooms; no more than 10 years old; 10-year sealed battery where battery units are allowed; hardwired alarms cannot be replaced with battery alarms
CO alarms less than 10 years old, in the hallway within 10 feet of all bedrooms
Homes with a low-voltage fire alarm system must have it tested by a certified alarm contractor before the inspection and show the certificate
House numbers at least 4 inches, numerals only, contrasting, on the house (not doors or mailboxes)
The Fire Marshal page says sale inspections check fire extinguishers too, but the June 2026 resale form and checklist do not list one

authorities.name: Haddon Township Bureau of Fire Prevention (Fire Marshal Office); the smoke/CO check is part of the township Resale COC inspection
authorities.lead_time: At least 14 business days before closing
authorities.how_to_apply: No separate smoke certificate application or fee was found. The Fire Marshal Office says it inspects all homes for sale for smoke alarms, CO alarms and fire extinguishers, and the township's Residential Resale / Tenant Change Inspection Application covers that (CSDCMAC) check together with the COC; see the resale_co fees ($150 and up). Submit the application with payment to the Annex Building, 10 Reeve Ave., at least 14 business days before closing.

evidence.quote: I understand that any change of ownership/occupancy including storage of personal property may not occur, prior to successful inspection & possession of a (CSDCMAC) inspection.
Inspect all homes for sale to ensure smoke detectors, carbon monoxide alarms, and fire extinguishers are installed and operating.
LOCAL ENFORCING AGENCY FOR: Haddon Township (Westmont, West Collingswood Heights, West Collingswood Extension) & Audubon Park.

fire_cert.notes: New this check: the Fire Marshal Office page can now be read. It says the Bureau of Fire Prevention inspects all homes for sale for smoke detectors, CO alarms and fire extinguishers, and that it is the local enforcing agency for Haddon Township and Audubon Park. Fire Marshals listed: William Behnke, Chief Fire Marshal / Official (ext. 6269, wbehnke@haddontwp.com) and Ryan Sheppard, Fire Marshal / Investigator (ext. 6276, rsheppard@haddontwp.com), who is also the Resale Inspector on the Construction & Zoning page. No separate smoke certificate form or fee is posted; the check is part of the resale COC. The DCA LEA registry (July 2026) lists Haddon Township as M (municipal), and the DCA directory lists 'Haddon Twp Constr' at 10 Reeve Av (856-854-1176) as the smoke detector compliance contact. The page's mention of fire extinguishers predates or ignores the 2025 state law (P.L.2025, c.19) that dropped the extinguisher from the sale requirement; the 2026 form does not list one.

other_items.label: Open permits must be closed
other_items.detail: Any work that needed a permit must have had one, with final inspections done and a Certificate of Approval issued.

other_items.label: Water meter
other_items.detail: Water meter must be installed, connected and accessible at inspection.

open_questions: Whether a fire extinguisher is still checked at the sale inspection (the Fire Marshal page says yes; the 2026 form does not list one; state law dropped it in 2025).
Which deadline the office uses: 14 business days (form and web page) or 30 days (Section 186-6), and whether the fee tiers count business days (form) or calendar days (code).
